proofs.proof_tex:
We first prove that the structural charts are exhaustive, independently of the target test.  By \(\mathrm{ass:selected\text{-}table\text{-}positivity}\), each entry of \(T_e\) and every \(v_e(z)\) is positive.  In any cycle factorization with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\),
\[
 T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top},
 \qquad a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z).                         \tag{19}
\]
The right side of (19) has rank at most two.  Hence a rank exceeding two makes the chart union and the cycle fiber empty, while positivity excludes rank zero.

Suppose first that \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=2\).  Define the observable normalized columns
\[
 c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\mathord\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}.
\]
Equation (19) gives
\[
 c_{ez}=\lambda_{ez}b_i+(1-\lambda_{ez})b_j,
 \qquad \lambda_{ez}=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1].       \tag{20}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\ne b_j\) and at least two distinct values of \(\lambda_{ez}\); consequently the affine hull of the observed \(c_{ez}\)'s is the line through \(b_i,b_j\).  Thus all observed columns lie in the closed segment \([b_i,b_j]\).  Conversely, if distinct simplex points \(b_i,b_j\) lie on that observed line and their segment contains every \(c_{ez}\), choose a coordinate \(h_e\) with \(b_i(h_e)\ne b_j(h_e)\) and put
\[
 a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
 \qquad
 a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z).                               \tag{21}
\]
Containment makes both coefficients nonnegative; (21) and the affine-line identity recover every column of \(T_e\), so (19) holds.  The two endpoint orders in \(\mathrm{thm:rank\text{-}two\text{-}orientation\text{-}atlas}\) exhaust the possibilities.  At each \(z\), positivity of \(v_e(z)\) leaves exactly three support states: \(a_{ei}(z)=0\), \(a_{ej}(z)=0\), or both are positive.  Their coordinatewise refinements therefore exhaust every rank-two support face.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=1\), \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\) proves that exactly one of the \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes holds.  In particular, modes \(\mathrm L\) and \(\mathrm R\) retain the inactive endpoint as a free simplex point subject only to its other incident cell, while mode \(\mathrm E\) retains the entire vector split \(s_e\).  The three coordinatewise alternatives \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\) exhaust its boundary faces.

Take the product of the four local lists and use one variable \(b_i\) for the two cells incident to response type \(i\).  Refine proxy supports, endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, coefficient supports, and each guarded pivot by their finitely many sign alternatives.  Formula (21) and the rank-one normal-form lemma place every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) in at least one such chart.  Conversely, direct substitution of the chart equations into (19), together with the simplex and nonnegativity atoms, places every chart point in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathcal C_A(T)=\bigcup_\chi X_\chi .                    \tag{22}
\]
This equality includes coincident endpoints, inactive rows, simultaneous rank-one cells, and forced-zero incident coefficients.

For design B, fix a chart in (22) and a positive projective vector \(\rho\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:iv\text{-}residual\text{-}forest}\), the two residuals incident to a response type must either both vanish or be nonzero and negatively proportional; a branch with exactly one zero residual is empty.  In an active branch, the lexicographically first nonzero coordinate and its sign give a finite pivot list and determine a positive ratio of incident margins.  The active subgraph of the response four-cycle is a forest unless all four links are active.  On a forest, ratios propagate from one positive scale per connected component.  When the whole cycle is active, propagation is consistent exactly when the product of the four oriented ratios equals one.  Positive scales and the single margin normalization give all and only the positive solutions.  Finally, the finite alternatives
\[
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)>0
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)<0,
 \qquad z<z',                                               \tag{23}
\]
are exhaustive for relevance.  The cited residual-forest theorem now proves that the refined union is exactly \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

Each \(X_\chi\) is a one-copy semialgebraic set over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\): every denominator cleared in constructing it is either a positive observed margin or a pivot whose nonzero sign is an atom of that chart.  The sampling and realizability algorithms in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}and\text{-}existential}\) therefore decide every chart's emptiness and return a real-univariate sample from any nonempty chart.  If all charts are empty, (22) and its design-B analogue prove incompatibility.  Otherwise choose one returned point \(x_0\), put \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and represent the ordered field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_{0,1},t_{0,2})\) by the cited primitive-element and Thom algorithms.  Because \(\tau_C\) is linear in the incident coefficient vectors, (18) adds one polynomial strict inequality of degree two and no new latent copy.  The cited existential algorithm decides each \(V_\chi(t_0)\) and samples it when nonempty.

If every \(V_\chi(t_0)\) is empty, then for arbitrary \(x\in X\) there is a chart \(X_\chi\) containing \(x\).  Its refinement is empty, so the nonnegative squared distance in (18) equals zero and \(\tau_C(x)=t_0\).  Hence \(\tau_C(X)=\{t_0\}\).  Conversely, if \(\tau_C(X)=\{t_0\}\), the strict inequality in (18) is false at every chart point, so every refinement is empty.  This proves the claimed equivalence without a connected-component decomposition.

As an exact smallest-face check, take every endpoint \(b_i\) equal to the uniform distribution on \(\mathcal W\) and every \(T_e\) equal to the product of that endpoint with the uniform \(v_e\) on \(\mathcal Z\).  Put every rank-one cell in mode \(\mathrm E\).  One legal cycle point uses each split \(s_e=v_e/2\).  For any rational \(0<\delta<1/2\), a second legal point replaces only
\[
 a_{11,2}=\left(\frac12+\delta\right)v_{11},
 \qquad
 a_{11,1}=\left(\frac12-\delta\right)v_{11}.
\]
All coefficients remain positive, every observed cell table is unchanged, and the first target coordinate changes from \(1/2\) to \(1/2+\delta\).  Thus the relevant set in (18) is nonempty on this coincident-endpoint support face, exactly as the global criterion declares.

If some \(V_\chi(t_0)\) is nonempty, its sampled point \(x_1\) satisfies \(\tau_C(x_1)\ne\tau_C(x_0)\) by (18).  The exact structural union makes both points legal cycle points, and \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) supplies two full SCMs with identical observables and, in design A, identical supplied margins.  If all refinements are empty, the sample representation of \(x_0\) supplies exact rational coordinate functions for \(t_0\) in one real algebraic primitive element.  The compiler emits a field expression only if exact arithmetic constructs one in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\); otherwise it retains the square-free real-univariate and Thom representation.  All branching predicates have coefficients generated by the observable input and the exactly represented \(t_0\), so the resulting compatibility and agreement certificates are observable.

For design A, \(\mathrm{lem:design\text{-}a\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonempty\text{-}criterion}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \hbox{and}\ 
 \mathcal C_A(T)\ne\varnothing.                           \tag{24}
\]
For design B, surjectivity in \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_B(T)\ne\varnothing.                           \tag{25}
\]
The exhaustive chart equalities in \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) make nonemptiness of either cycle fiber equivalent to nonemptiness of at least one of its finitely many structural charts.  Equations (24)--(25) therefore prove both incompatibility tests.  Since the cardinality of an empty target set is zero, an incompatible law is not rigid under \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}rigidity}\).

On a nonempty fiber, the same lift lemma preserves the target and is onto, whence
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)
 =\{\tau_C(x):x\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_B(p)
 =\{\tau_C(x):x\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.                      \tag{26}
\]
The mixed-support theorem proves that the applicable set on the right of (26) is \(\{t_0\}\) exactly when every chartwise disagreement set \(V_\chi(t_0)\) is empty.  Combining this equivalence with \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}rigidity}\) proves necessity and sufficiency of the stated observable tests.

When every disagreement set is empty, the sample \(x_0\) gives the common target, and the field-expression versus real-univariate/Thom output discipline follows from the exact representation in the mixed-support theorem.  When a disagreement set is nonempty, that theorem returns \(x_0,x_1\) with distinct cycle targets.  Equation (26) and \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) yield legal full SCMs with the same observable input and the same supplied \(m\) in design A.  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:interior\text{-}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}positive\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) gives strictly positive lifts precisely under the stated interior-chart premise.  Boundary witnesses remain legal by the general lift, but no unused positivity premise is imposed on them.

The factorization comparison in \(\mathrm{lem:shingaki\text{-}yoshida\text{-}kuroki\text{-}design\text{-}transfer}\) identifies the exact relationship between the two model descriptions.  Under \(P_{\vartheta}\in\mathfrak M\), response consistency restricts a selected cell \(e\) to the two types in \(\mathcal I_e\), proxy exclusion supplies one shared proxy kernel \(b_i\) for each type, and outcome-dependent selection contributes only a cell-specific factor.  Thus the selected law is the four-state response-type specialization of their Condition-1 factorization.  Requiring \(P_{\vartheta}(E)=m\) changes neither that factorization nor its regular identifying equations, so \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) is a fixed-margin subfiber.  Requiring \(Z\perp U\) imposes their equation-(13) common-\(Z\) restriction, while \(Z\not\!\perp X\) is exactly the additional relevance inequality in the present design-B fiber.

Let \(R_A(p)\) be the PN/PS pair supplied by Theorem 1 and Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) on the regular design-A domain.  By the cited transfer lemma, every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) satisfies
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_A(p).                                   \tag{27}
\]
This is restriction: fixing \(m\) merely selects a subset of the Condition-1 fiber.  If the subfiber is nonempty, (27) holds for all its members, and hence \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)=\{R_A(p)\}\).

Similarly, let \(R_B(p)\) denote the Corollary-1 value on the regular equation-(13) domain.  The cited lemma applies directly to every member of \(\mathcal F_B(p)\), so
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_B(p)
 \quad\hbox{for every }\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p),         \tag{28}
\]
and nonemptiness gives \(\mathcal T_B(p)=\{R_B(p)\}\).  The relevance requirement only restricts this identified equation-(13) fiber and therefore cannot change its common value.

By \(\mathrm{thm:full\text{-}rigidity\text{-}atlas}\), a nonempty fiber with either singleton target set in (27)--(28) passes every chartwise disagreement test and returns its unique value.  This proves agreement separately for regular design A and regular design B.

Outside the regular hypotheses, \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) proves that the chart family still exhausts every compatible rank-one or rank-two cycle factorization, including all named support faces and all design-B residual forests.  The full-rigidity theorem then returns the common exact target if every disagreement refinement is empty, and otherwise returns two target-changing full SCMs.  Equations (24)--(25) show that an empty chart union is reported as incompatibility before rigidity is asserted.

The extension of the compatible classification domain is strict.  Indeed, let \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), \(k=|\mathcal Z|\), and choose
\[
 \pi_i=\frac14,\qquad b_i(w)=\frac1\ell,\qquad
 g_i(z)=\frac1k,\qquad e_i(z)=\frac12,\qquad s_e=\frac12
\]
for every admissible index.  These normalized nonnegative mechanisms lie in \(\Theta\), obey response consistency, proxy exclusion, and outcome-dependent selection, and have \(c=1/2>0\).  Each observed cell has two incident response types, so direct multiplication gives
\[
 m_e=\frac14,\qquad
 p_{ewz}=\frac1{4k\ell}>0,
 \qquad T_e(w,z)=\frac1{k\ell}.
\]
Thus the resulting design-A fiber is compatible, while every \(T_e\) has rank one.  The regular proxy matrices therefore fail the invertibility requirement recorded in the cited design-transfer lemma, so this law lies outside the published regular domain but inside the atlas domain.  Finally, no step evaluates \(R_A\) or \(R_B\) after a regular denominator, rank, or separation condition fails; hence the additional conclusion strictly extends the compatible classification domain only, not the published formulas.

We verify the chart and format bounds in the order used by the revised compiler.

A vector \(b_i\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}\) has a nonempty support and hence at most \(2^{\ell}-1\) labeled support patterns.  The four response vertices contribute at most
\[
 (2^{\ell}-1)^4.                                           \tag{38}
\]
By selected-table positivity, \(v_e(z)>0\).  In a rank-two cell, the two orientations and the three coefficient-support states at each \(z\) give at most \(2\cdot3^k\) modes.  By \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), rank one contributes \(3^k\) coordinatewise faces in mode \(\mathrm E\) and the three further modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\).  Thus one cell contributes at most
\[
 2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3.                               \tag{39}
\]
There are four cells, so (38) times the fourth power of (39) proves the formula for \(M_A\).

For design B, each of the four response links has one zero-residual state or an active state recording one of \(k-1\) first nonbaseline pivots and one of two signs.  This gives \(2k-1\) states per link.  A relevance certificate chooses an unordered pair of distinct instrument values and one of two signs, giving \(2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1)\) possibilities.  Multiplication by the design-A count gives \(M_B\).  Adding the two design-specific families gives \(M_{k,\ell}\) in (29).  Endpoint incidences not fixed by these coarse modes remain polynomial atoms inside a chart, so they do not require an additional template multiplier.

For (30), the four endpoint vectors use \(4\ell\) coordinates and the two incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells use \(8k\).  In design B, projective common-instrument and optional \(q^X\) coordinates use at most \(2k\), while margins, response masses, and four transfer scales use at most twelve more.  Hence there are at most \(N_0=4\ell+10k+12\) variables.

There are \(4k\ell\) table-factorization equations.  Endpoint simplex and support conditions contribute at most \(4\ell+4\) atoms; coefficient simplex, zero-pattern, and split-face conditions contribute at most \(24k+8\); residual definitions and transfers contribute at most \(16k+8\); and optional proportionality minors contribute at most \(4(k-1)^2\).  Shared-instrument equations, all normalizations, endpoint incidences, cycle consistency, and signed relevance contribute fewer than \(20(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1)\) further atoms.  Since \(k\ge2\) and \(\ell\ge3\), their sum is no greater than \(S_0\).

The factorization and shared-instrument equations are bilinear.  A residual \(a_{ei}(z)-\rho_z a_{ei}(z_0)\) has degree at most two; an active-link transfer equation has degree at most three; the four-link product equation has degree four; and the relevance cross-product has degree at most three after the bilinear definition of \(q^X\) is substituted.  All remaining atoms have degree no larger.  Thus \(D_0=4\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}and\text{-}existential}\) to a chart of format \((N_0,S_0,D_0)\).  The bound \(\mathsf{Samp}\) decides emptiness and, for a nonempty chart, returns a sample whose real-univariate degree and record count are bounded by \((A_S,D_S)\), proving (31).  Only one such sample is retained as \(x_0\).  Its target \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\) lies in an ordered algebraic extension of degree at most \(D_S\), because \(\tau_C\) is a linear coordinate map.

For each chart the disagreement test adds exactly the one degree-two atom in (18).  It therefore has at most \(N_0\) variables, \(S_0+1\) atoms, degree at most \(D_0=4\), and coefficient-extension degree at most \(D_S\).  The cited existential algorithm gives the first pair in (32), with \(D_E\) measured over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Exact primitive-element conversion, square-free factorization, Thom comparison, and rational isolation give the second pair.  Across at most \(M_{k,\ell}\) charts, the product in (33) dominates the sum of all sampling, existential, and encoding records.  It also dominates \(D_S,D_E,D_R\) and their products, and hence every absolute algebraic degree created by a tower-to-primitive-element conversion.  This proves (33).

The cited singly-exponential bounds give, for a universal constant \(c\),
\[
 A_S+D_S
 \le (S_0+D_0+2)^{c(N_0+1)^c}.                            \tag{40}
\]
The same form applies to the existential stage over the algebraic coefficient extension; passing back to the original field multiplies its relative degree by at most \(D_S\).  Primitive-element and Thom normalization are singly exponential in the degrees and number of coordinates already produced.  Since \(N_0=O(Q)\), \(S_0=O(Q)\), \(D_0=4\), and \(M_{k,\ell}\le2^{Q^{c_0}}\) for a universal \(c_0\), every factor in (33) is bounded by \(2^{C_1Q^{C_1}}\).  A fixed product of such factors has the same form after increasing the universal constant, proving (34).

For arbitrary real \(\zeta\), chart coefficients belong to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\): normalization divides only by positive \(r_e\), and every later denominator is a chart pivot whose nonzero sign is recorded.  There are finitely many charts by (29).  The cited sampling, existential, sign, primitive-element, and root routines terminate relative to the stated field and order oracles.  Thus the full real-input computation terminates.

Now suppose the reduced observable coordinates are rational and have numerator and denominator binary length at most \(L\).  Reconstructing a deleted simplex coordinate and then forming any \(r_e\) adds at most \(4k\ell\le4Q\) rational coordinates.  Taking a common denominator therefore gives numerator and denominator lengths at most \(8Q(L+1)\).  Forming \(T_e=p_e/r_e\), multiplying at most four such coefficients in a chart polynomial, and adding at most \(S_0\) monomials is bounded by \(64Q^2(L+1)=h_0\).  This proves the initial height in (35).

The integer-height part of the cited sampling theorem gives \(h_S\).  The target coordinates are rational functions of the returned primitive element with height no greater than that bound after its coordinatewise monotone normalization.  Feeding the actual coefficient-extension degree \(D_S\) and height \(h_S\) into the existential algorithm gives \(h_E\); feeding both actual degrees and heights into the primitive-element, square-free, Thom, and isolation routines gives \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  This proves the sequential formulas (35)--(36), and the cited normalization algorithms give the asserted square-free integer and rational-isolating representations.

The cited height bounds have the form
\[
 h_{\mathrm{out}}
 \le (h_{\mathrm{in}}+1)^{2^{C_2Q^{C_2}}}                 \tag{41}
\]
at each of the fixed number of stages, after (40) and the extension degrees are substituted.  Composing a fixed number of powers in (41) multiplies their exponents, which remains at most \(2^{C_3Q^{C_3}}\).  Since \(h_0\le2^{C_3Q^{C_3}}(L+1)\), increasing the universal constant yields (37).  Thus every loop and every rational-input algebraic operation has an explicit finite bound.  The executed sequence is chart sampling followed by chartwise existential disagreement sampling; component and projection routines play no role in either the decision or these bounds.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(D\) be an effective ordered domain and let a semialgebraic subset of a real closed extension of the fraction field of \(D\) be given by a Boolean formula in \(n\) variables using at most \(s\) polynomial sign conditions of degree at most \(d\).  The critical-point and existential algorithms of Basu, Pollack, and Roy decide emptiness and, when the set is nonempty, return a real-univariate sample.  They remain effective over an explicitly ordered finite real-algebraic coefficient extension.  Primitive-element conversion, square-free factorization, Thom-sign determination, comparison, and rational root isolation give exact encodings over the original field.  There are explicit coordinatewise nondecreasing bounds \(\mathsf{Samp}\), \(\mathsf{Exist}\), and \(\mathsf{Enc}\) for record counts and absolute algebraic degrees, and corresponding integer-coefficient height bounds.  For a universal constant \(c\ge1\), the sampling and one-block existential record counts and relative degrees are bounded by
\[
 (s+d+2)^{c(n+1)^c},                                      \tag{42}
\]
with absolute degrees multiplied by at most the degree of the ordered coefficient extension.  If rational input coefficients have binary length at most \(h\), the output coefficients and rational isolating endpoints admit the conservative bound
\[
 (h+1)^{(s+d+2)^{c(n+1)^c}}.                              \tag{43}
\]
The same singly-exponential form, composed with the input algebraic degrees, applies to the stated encoding operations.

Their regular Conditions 2--3 impose the stated proxy-matrix invertibility and determinant-ratio separation requirements.  Under those conditions, Theorem 1 identifies PN and PS and Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) derive the reported observable formulas.  Their equation (13) is the common-instrument, instrument-exogenous subclass, and Corollary 1 gives the corresponding regular IV-design identification.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), there is a one-copy structural compiler \(\mathscr A\) with the following properties.  It rejects a cell rank exceeding two.  Every rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient support faces.  Every rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), with the \(\mathrm E\) split refined coordinatewise.  Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex and are refined by proxy supports, endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and nonzero pivots.  Writing \(X_\chi\) for a resulting chart and \(X=\bigcup_\chi X_\chi\), the union is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at every response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, the active-cycle product-one equation, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives a finite chart union equal exactly to \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

The compiler tests every \(X_\chi\) for emptiness.  If the union is nonempty, exact one-copy sampling supplies \(x_0\in X\), and the compiler sets \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\).  It then tests, separately for every chart,
\[
 V_\chi(t_0)=\left\{x\in X_\chi:
 \bigl(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1}\bigr)^2+
 \bigl(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2}\bigr)^2>0\right\}.             \tag{18}
\]
The target image \(\tau_C(X)\) is a singleton if and only if every set in (18) is empty.  A nonempty refinement directly supplies a sampled \(x_1\) with \(\tau_C(x_1)\ne t_0\), and the two cycle points lift to legal target-changing full SCMs.  Thus the decision uses one sampled feasible point and one-copy existential realizability on each structural chart; it uses neither connected-component enumeration nor target projection, although either may be computed as an optional diagnostic.

Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the calculation is relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  The tests in (18) are performed over the ordered finite extension \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_{0,1},t_{0,2})\).  A rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when that expression is constructed; otherwise it is returned by a real-univariate representation and Thom data over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current statement makes connected-component enumeration and target projection mandatory even though global constancy follows from one feasible sample and a one-copy existential disagreement test on each exhaustive chart. The replacement removes that unnecessary procedural burden while preserving the full structural union and every causal certificate.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\) and every structural chart for \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  If the margin test fails or all charts are empty, then \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\), and the law is not rigid under \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\).  Otherwise the compiler samples \(x_0\in\mathcal C_A(T)\), sets \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and design A is rigid if and only if every chartwise disagreement set \(V_\chi(t_0)\) in (18) is empty.  For design B, all structural charts are empty if and only if \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\varnothing\); otherwise a sampled \(x_0\in\mathcal C_B(T)\) gives \(t_0\), and design B is rigid if and only if every corresponding residual-forest chartwise disagreement set is empty.  These are finite observable rank, support, incidence, residual-cycle, and exact realizability tests.

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid \(t_0\) is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data.  For rational \(\zeta\), the representation may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval.  Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and identical supplied margins when margins are supplied, but different \(\tau\).  If both sampled cycle witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity conclusion is asserted for a witness on a boundary face.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current classifier is phrased in component-agreement terms. The replacement states the strictly leaner decision contract actually proved: sample one feasible point and rule out target disagreement on every chart.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
At the selected-law factorization level, \(\mathfrak M\) is the finite four-response-type specialization of Condition 1 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026).  Design A, \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), is the subfiber obtained by fixing the population cell margin \(m\); consequently Theorem 1 of that paper transfers to the regular design-A domain by restriction.  Design B, \(\mathcal F_B(p)\), is the equation-(13) IV subclass with the additional relevance inequality; consequently Corollary 1 transfers directly to its regular domain.  On every such regular observable law for which the applicable full fiber is nonempty, the fiber is rigid and \(\mathscr A\) returns the corresponding published PN/PS value, including the Appendix formulas (A.28)--(A.33) where they apply.

The atlas additionally classifies every compatible observable law in the singular or boundary complement of those regular domains, including design-A rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, and forced-zero incident coefficients, and the analogous design-B residual-forest strata.  It returns either an exact target-rigidity certificate or a legal target-changing full-SCM pair.  An empty fiber is reported separately as incompatibility. \[

 \bigl(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1}\bigr)^2+
 \bigl(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2}\bigr)^2>0\right\}.
\]
If every refinement is empty, return \(t_0\); if one is nonempty, sample it and lift the resulting pair into \(\mathcal F_A\) or \(\mathcal F_B\). proposed.statement:
For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), there is a one-copy structural compiler \(\mathscr A\) with the following properties.  It rejects a cell rank exceeding two.  Every rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient support faces.  Every rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), with the \(\mathrm E\) split refined coordinatewise.  Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex and are refined by proxy supports, endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and nonzero pivots.  Writing \(X_\chi\) for a resulting chart and \(X=\bigcup_\chi X_\chi\), the union is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at every response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, the active-cycle product-one equation, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives a finite chart union equal exactly to \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

The compiler tests every \(X_\chi\) for emptiness.  If the union is nonempty, exact one-copy sampling supplies \(x_0\in X\), and the compiler sets \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\).  It then tests, separately for every chart,
\[
 V_\chi(t_0)=\left\{x\in X_\chi:
 \bigl(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1}\bigr)^2+
 \bigl(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2}\bigr)^2>0\right\}.             \tag{18}
\]
The target image \(\tau_C(X)\) is a singleton if and only if every set in (18) is empty.  A nonempty refinement directly supplies a sampled \(x_1\) with \(\tau_C(x_1)\ne t_0\), and the two cycle points lift to legal target-changing full SCMs.  Thus the decision uses one sampled feasible point and one-copy existential realizability on each structural chart; it uses neither connected-component enumeration nor target projection, although either may be computed as an optional diagnostic.

Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the calculation is relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  The tests in (18) are performed over the ordered finite extension \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_{0,1},t_{0,2})\).  A rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when that expression is constructed; otherwise it is returned by a real-univariate representation and Thom data over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).
proposed.justification: This theorem closes the structural gap and gives a globally complete one-sample rigidity decision over the exhaustive chart union.
proposed.gap: Earlier rounds retained a correct chart atlas but imposed unnecessary connected-component description and target-projection stages.
proposed.consumer: The global atlas and inference procedures receive an exact target, legal twins, or incompatibility from one-copy chart realizability alone.

proposed.statement:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\) and every structural chart for \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  If the margin test fails or all charts are empty, then \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\), and the law is not rigid under \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\).  Otherwise the compiler samples \(x_0\in\mathcal C_A(T)\), sets \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and design A is rigid if and only if every chartwise disagreement set \(V_\chi(t_0)\) in (18) is empty.  For design B, all structural charts are empty if and only if \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\varnothing\); otherwise a sampled \(x_0\in\mathcal C_B(T)\) gives \(t_0\), and design B is rigid if and only if every corresponding residual-forest chartwise disagreement set is empty.  These are finite observable rank, support, incidence, residual-cycle, and exact realizability tests.

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid \(t_0\) is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data.  For rational \(\zeta\), the representation may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval.  Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and identical supplied margins when margins are supplied, but different \(\tau\).  If both sampled cycle witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity conclusion is asserted for a witness on a boundary face.
proposed.justification: The theorem is the exact necessary-and-sufficient causal target classifier, with incompatibility separated from nonrigidity.
proposed.gap: Regular proxy inversion does not decide global target agreement across all mixed-rank and support-face charts.
proposed.consumer: Analysts receive an exact target, a legal target-changing SCM pair, or an incompatibility certificate without a component decomposition.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, a boundary-complete structural atlas decides PN/PS target rigidity. It exhausts rank-two orientations and the four disjoint rank-one modes, retains equal-endpoint split vectors and inactive rows, and adds response-level residual forests for the unknown-margin relevant-IV design. After chartwise compatibility tests, one feasible cycle point is sampled and each chart is tested for a different target by one-copy existential realizability. The output is an exact common target, two legal same-observable SCMs, or model incompatibility; connected-component enumeration and target projection are optional diagnostics. The selected-law model is the finite four-response-type specialization of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki Condition 1: design A is its fixed-margin subfiber and design B is its equation-(13) IV subclass plus relevance. Theorem 1 transfers by restriction in design A and Corollary 1 transfers directly in design B. The contribution is the strict compatible singular/boundary classification extension, not an extension of those regular formulas. Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains universal, while Wald and Hausdorff equivalence remain confined to separated, locally saturated rigid profiles.

project_justification.gap: Published regular proxy formulas identify PN and PS under their rank and separation conditions but do not classify compatible fibers when ranks fall, coefficients reach support faces, endpoints coincide, rows become inactive, or shared-instrument equations couple unknown margins. Generic real-algebraic decidability also hides the response-cycle obstruction and can impose unnecessary decomposition stages.
project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled cycle whose causal target may be rigid even while nuisance factorizations vary. Exhaustive local edge modes, shared endpoints, and residual forests reduce each legal fiber to a finite union of one-copy semialgebraic charts. One feasible target value then turns global rigidity into one existential disagreement test per chart.
project_justification.fill: The compiler gives necessary and sufficient compatibility and target-agreement tests for supplied-margin and relevant-IV designs. It samples one feasible chart point, tests every chart for a different target, and returns an exact algebraic value or legal full-SCM twins. Its fixed-alphabet termination theorem multiplies the causal chart count by sequential singly-exponential sampling, existential, and encoding bounds, with coefficient-extension degree and rational height propagated in execution order. The statistical layer remains separated-chart Wald inference together with universal finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage.

prose_updates.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026) provide the selected response-type model and regular PN/PS formulas. At selected-law factorization level, the present finite model is their Condition-1 four-response-type specialization. The supplied-margin design is a fixed-margin subfiber, so their Theorem 1 transfers by restriction; the unknown-margin IV design is their equation-(13) subclass plus relevance, so their Corollary 1 transfers directly. The atlas agrees on those exact regular overlaps and extends only the compatible classification domain to singular and boundary fibers; it neither extends the regular formulas beyond their hypotheses nor claims blanket subsumption. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) and Kawakami (2021) supply separate regular overlap checks, including a one-law boundary scope separation from Kawakami's invertibility domain. Nonnegative-factorization rigidity work informs the geometry but does not state causal target constancy on this labeled cycle. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the classical singly-exponential critical-point sampling, one-block existential-realizability, primitive-element, Thom-sign, and isolation algorithms used after structural exhaustiveness is proved.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact compiler is a theorem-level symbolic procedure, not a completed production implementation or a favorable growing-alphabet complexity claim. The displayed fixed-alphabet envelope uses published singly-exponential bounds for the executed sampling and existential stages, composed with algebraic coefficient-extension and height bounds; optional connected-component or target-projection diagnostics are excluded. Over arbitrary real observables, computation is relative to effective arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles. A rational field expression is returned only when constructed; otherwise the exact output remains a real-univariate and Thom encoding. Strictly positive twins are guaranteed only when both sampled cycle witnesses occupy interior support charts. Universal confidence coverage does not imply shrinking at a nonidentified transition, and first-order Hausdorff agreement still requires a locally saturated separated rigid profile. The frozen materials lack the released numerical GEUVADIS count table and binarization thresholds, so no empirical compatibility or rigidity verdict is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The mathematical contribution is the exhaustive fixed-alphabet response-cycle classifier and its one-sample, all-chart existential agreement test. Empty fibers are incompatibility and are non-rigid under the cardinality-one definition. The selected model matches the published Condition-1 factorization only at the stated finite four-response-type specialization; design A restricts it by fixed margins, and design B restricts equation (13) by relevance. Published regular values transfer on those precise subfibers, while the new result strictly extends compatible classification to singular and boundary strata without extending the published formula or claiming blanket subsumption. The termination result gives an explicit chart count and sequential sampling, existential, encoding, degree, and rational-height bounds, not favorable growing-alphabet complexity. Wald inference still requires chart separation, common first derivatives, smooth continuations, proportional margin sampling when applicable, and nonsingular target covariance. Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains unchanged and universal; its optional Wald-equivalence clause still additionally requires a locally saturated compatible neighborhood. The GEUVADIS application remains an audit protocol conditional on the graph and recovery of the released table, not a numerical reanalysis.
